20	// findingColumns describes the findings table.
21	//
22	// The table opens on the order the scanner reported — `SortColumn: -1`, which
23	// datatable keeps as a stop on the cycle, so `.` always leads back to it. Every
24	// column sorts, because `.` was handed back to the sort when the severity floor
25	// became four tokens (§3.26) and then no column was ever given a `Less`:
26	// CycleSort returned on its first line and the header advertised a key that did
27	// nothing at all.
28	//
29	// Three columns search, and that is not optional either. Declaring tokens makes
30	// `Searchable()` true, so `/` already opened a query — against no searchable
31	// column, which matches nothing and empties the table. The bar's own left half
32	// says `/ search...` whether or not anything answers it.
33	//
34	// Severity searches nothing on purpose: c/h/m/l are the severity filter, and a
35	// second way to ask one question is what this codebase spends its time
36	// removing. The Title is not pre-truncated either — bubbles cuts every cell to
37	// its column width with the same ellipsis, and doing it by hand at width-3
38	// first only cost three characters of title.
39	func findingColumns() []datatable.Column[scan.Finding] {
40		return []datatable.Column[scan.Finding]{
41			{
42				Title: "Severity", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, MinWidth: 10,
43				Cell: func(f scan.Finding) string { return string(f.Severity) },
44				// The same palette the selected row uses, so a severity reads the
45				// same colour whether or not the cursor is on it.
46				Style: func(f scan.Finding) lipgloss.Style { return theme.SeverityTextStyle(string(f.Severity)) },
47				Less:  func(a, b scan.Finding) bool { return severityRank(a.Severity) < severityRank(b.Severity) },
48			},
49			{
50				Title: "ID", Sizing: datatable.SizingContent, MinWidth: 18,
51				Cell:   func(f scan.Finding) string { return f.ID },
52				Less:   func(a, b scan.Finding) bool { return a.ID < b.ID },
53				Search: func(f scan.Finding) string { return f.ID },
54			},
55			{
56				Title: "Title", Sizing: datatable.SizingContent, MinWidth: 20, Flex: 1,
57				// The Pod Security label is a prefix of the text (DEVDESK-686); the
58				// sort stays on the title and the search sees the label.
59				Cell:   titleWithLabel,
60				Less:   func(a, b scan.Finding) bool { return a.Title < b.Title },
61				Search: func(f scan.Finding) string { return titleWithLabel(f) + " " + f.PkgName + " " + f.File },
62			},
63			{
64				Title: "Source", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, Optional: true, MinWidth: 14,
65				Cell:   sourceDisplay,
66				Less:   func(a, b scan.Finding) bool { return sourceDisplay(a) < sourceDisplay(b) },
67				Search: sourceDisplay,
68			},
69			{
70				// Appended last, so the indices above do not move. No Less and no
71				// Search: the Title search already matches the file, and a second
72				// way to ask the same question is noise. It keeps the end of a long
73				// path, which is what tells two findings apart.
74				Title: "File", Sizing: datatable.SizingContent, MinWidth: 16, MaxWidth: 40,
75				Optional: true, TruncateHead: true,
76				Cell: fileCell,
77			},
78		}
79	}
80	
81	// fileColumn is the index of the File column in findingColumns.
82	const fileColumn = 4
83	
84	// fileCell is the File cell: plain text (Rule 122), with the scanner container's
85	// mount removed and a path under HOME folded. The columns are built once, before
86	// any result exists, so the cell does not know the scanned target (the detail
87	// does): an absolute path under the target shows as the folded absolute path here
88	// and as a relative one in the detail. Trivy reports relative paths, so this is
89	// the rare case.
90	func fileCell(f scan.Finding) string { return shortPaths(f.File, "") }
91	
92	// severityRank orders the levels by how bad they are, which is the only order
93	// worth sorting this column by: alphabetically, CRITICAL lands between no two
94	// levels it belongs with — HIGH, LOW, MEDIUM — so a descending sort would put
95	// MEDIUM at the top and bury the finding the user opened the view for.
96	//
97	// Ascending is least-severe-first, so `.`'s second press (descending, Rule 111)
98	// is the one that answers "what is worst here".
99	//
100	// UNKNOWN ranks below LOW rather than above CRITICAL: it is what a scanner
101	// says when it has no score, not a claim that something is worse than critical.
102	// It has no token either, for the same reason — see severityToken.
103	func severityRank(s scan.SeverityLevel) int {
104		switch s {
105		case scan.SeverityCritical:
106			return 4
107		case scan.SeverityHigh:
108			return 3
109		case scan.SeverityMedium:
110			return 2
111		case scan.SeverityLow:
112			return 1
113		default:
114			return 0
115		}
116	}
117	
118	// findingSelectedStyles colours the selected row by the severity under the
119	// cursor. It is what refreshSelectionStyle did, minus its own bounds check.
120	func findingSelectedStyles(f scan.Finding) table.Styles {
121		return theme.TableStylesForSeverity(string(f.Severity))
122	}
123	
124	// Tab constants for results view
125	const (
126		TabCVE       = 0
127		TabSecrets   = 1
128		TabLicense   = 2
129		TabMisconfig = 3
130		TabCIScore   = 4
131		// TabRemediation is not a category of finding: it has no entry in
132		// tabCategory and its body is its own table (remediation.go).
133		TabRemediation = 5
134		tabCount       = 6
135	)
136	
137	// updateFindingsTable populates the findings table based on active tab and filters.
138	//
139	// The tab is this view's own filter, not the component's: it selects which
140	// findings exist at all, where a FilterBar query narrows a list that is already
141	// settled. The severity went the other way — it is four cumulative tokens the
142	// table owns (Rule 136), which is what gave `.` back to the sort.
143	func (m *Model) updateFindingsTable() {
144		if m.result == nil {
145			return
146		}
147	
148		m.findingsTable.SetItems(m.filterFindingsByTab())
149		// A change of tab or severity is a change of scope, not a shorter list, so
150		// the cursor goes back to the top and the columns are measured again.
151		// SetItems deliberately does neither on its own.
152		m.findingsTable.GotoTop()
153		m.findingsTable.Remeasure()
154	}
155	
156	// tabCategory maps a tab to the finding category it shows.
157	//
158	// The tabs and scan.Result's counters are now the same classification, applied
159	// once in scan.Categorize: they were two rules that disagreed on three inputs,
160	// each of which produced a finding counted in the header but present in no tab
161	// at all — visible nowhere, which is the worst way for a finding to be wrong.
162	var tabCategory = map[int]scan.Category{
163		TabCVE:       scan.CategoryVulnerability,
164		TabSecrets:   scan.CategorySecret,
165		TabLicense:   scan.CategoryLicense,
166		TabMisconfig: scan.CategoryMisconfiguration,
167		TabCIScore:   scan.CategoryCIScore,
168	}
169	
170	// filterFindingsByTab returns findings filtered by the active tab
171	func (m *Model) filterFindingsByTab() []scan.Finding {
172		if m.result == nil {
173			return nil
174		}
175	
176		want, ok := tabCategory[m.activeTab]
177		if !ok {
178			return nil
179		}
180		var filtered []scan.Finding
181		for _, f := range m.result.Findings {
182			if scan.Categorize(f) == want {
183				filtered = append(filtered, f)
184			}
185		}
186		return filtered
187	}
188	
189	// sourceDisplay returns a display string for the source column.
190	//
191	// Which tool found it, not which category it is — the tab already says the
192	// category, and telling gitleaks from trivy-secret in the Secrets tab is the
193	// point of showing both there.
194	//
195	// A Trivy misconfiguration shows its dialect instead (§3.80): "misconfig"
196	// only repeated the tab's name, while "kubernetes", "helm" or "dockerfile"
197	// is what tells a Deployment's rule from a Dockerfile's on a tab that lists
198	// both — and it is searchable, so `/helm` narrows to the charts. A column of
199	// its own was the alternative, but every other tab would have carried it
200	// empty. A result cached before the dialect was recorded keeps "misconfig".
201	func sourceDisplay(f scan.Finding) string {
202		switch f.Source {
203		case scan.SourceTrivyLicense:
204			return "license"
205		case scan.SourceTrivyMisconfig:
206			if f.IaCType != "" {
207				return f.IaCType
208			}
209			return "misconfig"
210		case scan.SourceKubeconform:
211			// Schema validation, which is what separates it from Trivy's
212			// kubernetes findings on the same manifest.
213			return "schema"
214		case scan.SourceHelm:
215			// Not "helm": that is already the dialect of Trivy's chart findings.
216			return "helm lint"
217		case scan.SourceKustomize:
218			return "kustomize"
219		case scan.SourceBuildContext:
220			// DevDesk's own check (§3.81): what a COPY of the whole context takes
221			// into the image, which no scanner reports.
222			return "context"
223		case scan.SourceGitleaks:
224			return "gitleaks"
225		case scan.SourceTrivySecret:
226			return "trivy"
227		case scan.SourceTrivy:
228			return "vuln"
229		default:
230			return f.Source
231		}
232	}
233	
234	// countFindingsByTab returns the count of findings for each tab. These are the
235	// numbers on the tab labels, and scan.Result's counters are the same ones.
236	func (m *Model) countFindingsByTab() (cve, secrets, licenses, misconfigs, ci int) {
237		if m.result == nil {
238			return 0, 0, 0, 0, 0
239		}
240	
241		for _, f := range m.result.Findings {
242			switch scan.Categorize(f) {
243			case scan.CategoryVulnerability:
244				cve++
245			case scan.CategorySecret:
246				secrets++
247			case scan.CategoryLicense:
248				licenses++
249			case scan.CategoryMisconfiguration:
250				misconfigs++
251			case scan.CategoryCIScore:
252				ci++
253			}
254		}
255		return cve, secrets, licenses, misconfigs, ci
256	}
257	
258	// enterTab is what entering a tab starts: the Dockerfile read of the
259	// Remediation tab, the invalid-setting warning of the Misconfigurations one.
260	func (m *Model) enterTab() tea.Cmd {
261		return tea.Batch(m.enterRemediationTab(), m.enterPSSTab())
262	}
263	
264	// enterRemediationTab reads the Dockerfiles when the tab just switched to is the
265	// Remediation one, and does nothing on any other.
266	func (m *Model) enterRemediationTab() tea.Cmd {
267		if m.activeTab != TabRemediation {
268			return nil
269		}
270		return m.enterRemediation()
271	}
272	
273	// switchTab switches to the given tab index and refreshes the table
274	func (m *Model) switchTab(tab int) {
275		m.activeTab = tab
276		// The Pod Security filter belongs to one visit of the Misconfigurations
277		// tab: it is off on the way in and on the way out.
278		// Only when it is on: switching off an off token rebuilds the rows and
279		// measures the columns again for nothing.
280		if m.findingsTable.IsTokenActive(pssToken) {
281			m.findingsTable.SetTokenActive(pssToken, false)
282		}
283		// The CI tab carries a score line above the table, so the height changes
284		// with the tab and not only with the window.
285		m.resizeFindings()
286		m.footer.Clear()
287		m.updateFindingsTable()
288	}
289	
290	// handleIgnoreSecret prompts confirmation to ignore a secret finding.
291	//
292	// Gitleaks findings only. .gitleaksignore is matched on a Gitleaks fingerprint,
293	// which a Trivy secret does not have — AddToGitleaksIgnore would fabricate one
294	// from the file and rule, write it, and report success for a line Gitleaks will
295	// never match and Trivy never reads. Refusing says so instead.
296	func (m Model) handleIgnoreSecret() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
297		if exclude := m.canExclude(); !exclude.Enabled() {
298			return m, m.footer.Warn(exclude.Reason)
299		}
300		finding, _ := m.subjectFinding()
301		m.findingToIgnore = &finding
302		m.confirmModal = sharedcomponents.NewConfirmModal(
303			"Ignore Secret",
304			fmt.Sprintf("Add this secret to .gitleaksignore?\n\nFile: %s\nRule: %s", finding.File, finding.ID),
305		)
306		return m, nil
307	}
308	
309	// The two findings actions, and why each does not apply (Rule 130).
310	const (
311		reasonNoFinding    = "No finding selected"
312		reasonNotASecret   = "REDACTED"
313		reasonNotGitleaks  = "Only Gitleaks findings can be added to .gitleaksignore"
314		reasonNotCITab     = "The resolved pipeline belongs to the CI tab"
315		reasonNotARepo     = "An image has no pipeline"
316		reasonNoResolution = "This forge does not resolve a pipeline server-side"
317		reasonNothingToSee = "No finding to open"
318	)
319	
320	// canOpenFinding reports whether enter has a row to detail.
321	func (m Model) canOpenFinding() shortcut.Availability {
322		if _, ok := m.findingsTable.Selected(); !ok {
323			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNothingToSee)
324		}
325		return shortcut.Availability{}
326	}
327	
328	// canExclude reports whether X applies to the selected finding.
329	//
330	// .gitleaksignore is matched on a Gitleaks fingerprint, which a Trivy secret
331	// does not have — fabricating one would report success for a line nothing will
332	// ever match. The tab is checked first because it is the coarser answer: on
333	// the CVE tab the key means nothing at all, whatever the row.
334	// openPipelineKey opens the pipeline the forge resolves for this repository.
335	//
336	// It is a **declared exception** to the uppercase vocabulary
337	// (keymap.DeclaredExceptions), on the precedent of `c` in oci/network-inspect
338	// and for the reason written there: the action exists on one sub-screen, and
339	// burning one of the three remaining free capitals for it would cost more than
340	// it returns.
341	//
342	// `o` and not `p`: `o` already means "open what this screen points at" in this
343	// view's details state, where it opens a finding's reference. One verb, two
344	// screens, and the shortcut column is replaced by the mode either way.
345	const openPipelineKey = "o"
346	
347	// canOpenPipeline decides whether the resolved pipeline can be fetched.
348	//
349	// The tab is checked first for canExclude's reason — it is the coarser answer,
350	// and off the CI tab the key means nothing whatever the row. The shape is
351	// checked before anything is read: a GitHub context cannot answer this at all,
352	// and finding that out after a keystroke and a git call would be worse than
353	// saying so in the column.
354	func (m Model) canOpenPipeline() shortcut.Availability {
355		switch {
356		case m.activeTab != TabCIScore:
357			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNotCITab)
358		case m.result == nil || m.result.TargetType != scan.TargetDirectory:
359			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNotARepo)
360		case !forge.ShapeFor(m.config.Forge.Type).MergedCIConfig:
361			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNoResolution)
362		}
363		return shortcut.Availability{}
364	}
365	
366	// openResolvedPipeline hands the document to the router, which opens the
367	// viewer on it. The fetch is the source's, so it runs on the viewer's own Cmd
368	// (Rule 110) and its failures are reported where the document would have been.
369	func (m Model) openResolvedPipeline() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
370		// The refusal is never silent (Rule 130), and it is a Warn rather than an
371		// Error: nothing failed, the key does not apply as asked (Rule 128). The
372		// reason is the one canOpenPipeline computed, so the footer and the greyed
373		// entry cannot be about different things.
374		if a := m.canOpenPipeline(); !a.Enabled() {
375			return m, m.footer.Warn(a.Reason)
376		}
377		source := pipelineSource{
378			RepoPath: m.result.Target,
379			Label:    theme.FoldHome(m.result.Target),
380			Forge:    m.config.Forge,
381			Secrets:  m.secrets,
382			Findings: m.result.Findings,
383		}
384		return m, func() tea.Msg { return uiviewer.OpenRequestMsg{Source: source} }
385	}
386	
387	func (m Model) canExclude() shortcut.Availability {
388		if m.activeTab != TabSecrets {
389			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNotASecret)
390		}
391		finding, ok := m.subjectFinding()
392		switch {
393		case !ok:
394			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNoFinding)
395		case finding.Source != scan.SourceGitleaks:
396			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNotGitleaks)
397		}
398		return shortcut.Availability{}
399	}
400	
401	// handleResultsState processes input in results state.
402	//
403	// The search answers first, and every key below is unreachable while it has the
404	// keyboard: "c" is a character in a query, "esc" cancels the search rather than
405	// leaving the results, and "enter" confirms it rather than opening a finding.
406	// The inventory has had this guard since it gained a bar; this state gained one
407	// the day the severity floor became tokens, and never got the guard with it.
408	func (m Model) handleResultsState(msg tea.KeyPressMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
409		if m.findingsTable.InEditMode() {
410			return m, m.findingsTable.Update(msg)
411		}
412		if m.activeTab == TabRemediation {
413			if next, cmd, handled := m.handleRemediationKey(msg); handled {
414				return next, cmd
415			}
416		}
417		switch msg.String() {
418		case "esc":
419			// No origin view means this view was opened directly, so esc stays
420			// inside it and goes back to whichever landing state it opened on.
421			if m.OriginView == "" {
422				return m.goHome()
423			}
424			return m, func() tea.Msg { return BackToOriginMsg{Origin: m.OriginView} }
425		case "enter":
426			var preview tea.Cmd
427			if finding, ok := m.findingsTable.Selected(); ok {
428				// The details view is about a finding, not about a row index — an
429				// index would name a different one the moment the list changed
430				// under it, which is how workspaces got D24.
431				m.selectedFinding = &finding
432				m.state = StateDetails
433				m.sizeDetails()
434				preview = m.startChangePreview()
435				m.detailsViewport.SetContent(m.buildDetailsContent())
436				m.detailsViewport.GotoTop()
437			}
438			return m, preview
439		case "ctrl+r":
440			m.activeTab = TabCVE
441			return m.goHome()
442		case "tab":
443			m.switchTab((m.activeTab + 1) % tabCount)
444			cmd := m.enterTab()
445			return m, cmd
446		case "shift+tab":
447			m.switchTab((m.activeTab + tabCount - 1) % tabCount)
448			cmd := m.enterTab()
449			return m, cmd
450		// 1-4 jumped straight to a tab. They were the application's only numeric
451		// bindings, and an exception in a single view is precisely what §3.26
452		// dismantles — tab reaches all four.
453		case "c", "h", "m", "l":
454			return m.toggleSeverity(msg.String())
455		case pssFilterKey:
456			return m.togglePSS()
457		case keymap.Exclude:
458			return m.handleIgnoreSecret()
459		case openPipelineKey:
460			return m.openResolvedPipeline()
461		case keymap.Scan:
462			// Off the Remediation tab this refuses, with the reason (Rule 130).
463			return m.scanCandidates()
464		case writeRemediationKey:
465			// One key, one verb — write the file — applied to whichever tab's
466			// object. The Remediation tab writes a base image, the
467			// Misconfigurations tab a built-in fix; anywhere else the refusal says
468			// which tab it belongs to (Rule 130).
469			if m.activeTab == TabMisconfig {
470				return m.prepareMisconfigFix()
471			}
472			return m.prepareRemediationWrite()
473		}
474		// `.` is the sort again, and the search and the severity tokens are the
475		// table's (Rule 136).
476		return m, m.findingsTable.Update(msg)
477	}
478	
479	// toggleSeverity flips one severity token. Cumulative: c and h together ask for
480	// "CRITICAL or HIGH", which is the question a threshold cycle could not put.
481	func (m Model) toggleSeverity(key string) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
482		label := map[string]string{"c": "critical", "h": "high", "m": "medium", "l": "low"}[key]
483		m.findingsTable.SetTokenActive(label, !m.findingsTable.IsTokenActive(label))
484		m.findingsTable.GotoTop()
485		return m, nil
486	}
487	
488	// resizeFindings lays the findings table out. Every tab gets the whole height:
489	// the CI tab used to give two rows to a score line above the table, and losing
490	// two findings on one tab out of five — for a letter the inventory already
491	// carries per target — was not worth the jump on every tab switch.
492	func (m *Model) resizeFindings() {
493		// The File column belongs to the Misconfigurations tab: the same rule
494		// there can fire in many files, and nowhere else it says nothing more than
495		// the title. Done here, with the size, so a tab switch and a resize cannot
496		// disagree.
497		m.findingsTable.SetColumnHidden(fileColumn, m.activeTab != TabMisconfig)
498		m.findingsTable.Resize(m.width, max(m.height, 5))
499		m.remediation.table.Resize(m.width, max(m.height, 5))
500	}

1	package security
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"strings"
6	
7		tea "charm.land/bubbletea/v2"
8		"charm.land/lipgloss/v2"
9	
10		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/command"
11		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/jobs"
12		sharedcomponents "github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/components"
13		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/indicator"
14		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
15	)
16	
17	// View is the Bubble Tea v2 face of Render: the content only. The terminal
18	// state (alternate screen, colours) belongs to whoever owns the program.
19	func (m Model) View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }
20	
21	// Render renders the UI
22	func (m Model) Render() string {
23		// Show whichever modal is active (Rule 112: modals confirm, forms fill the
24		// viewport).
25		if modal := m.modalView(); modal != "" {
26			return lipgloss.Place(
27				m.width, m.height,
28				lipgloss.Center, lipgloss.Center,
29				modal,
30				lipgloss.WithWhitespaceStyle(lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground)),
31			)
32		}
33	
34		switch m.state {
35		case StateInventory:
36			return m.renderInventoryView()
37		case StateResults:
38			return m.renderResultsView()
39		case StateDetails:
40			return m.renderDetailsView()
41		}
42		return ""
43	}
44	
45	// renderResultsView renders the results summary
46	func (m Model) renderResultsView() string {
47		if m.result == nil {
48			return "No results"
49		}
50	
51		// A stage that failed is **not** rendered here. It goes to the log, and the
52		// footer says to look there (Rule 128).
53		//
54		// It used to be a panel that replaced the whole table whenever
55		// Result.Errors was non-empty, on the stated grounds that a failed scan has
56		// no partial results to browse. That held while an error meant nothing had
57		// run; it stopped holding the day a stage could fail beside three that
58		// succeeded, and a plumber failure then took every CVE and every secret
59		// down with it. Folding it to a banner above the table only moved the
60		// problem — five tabs, permanently, for a message read once — and a tool's
61		// stderr reformatted for a viewport is what a log is for.
62		//
63		// Nothing is lost by it: internal/scan logs every stage failure at the
64		// point it records one, which it did not do before. The only copy of the
65		// reason used to be on screen.
66		//
67		// The grade had a line of its own above the table on the CI tab, and it is
68		// gone: it cost that tab two of its rows — the line and its blank — on
69		// every open, to state a letter the inventory's own CI column carries per
70		// target. A tab that shows fewer findings than its four neighbours, for a
71		// value already on the previous screen, is not a trade worth making.
72		if m.activeTab == TabRemediation {
73			return m.remediation.table.View()
74		}
75		return m.findingsTable.View()
76	}
77	
78	// GetFooterHeight returns the footer height for this view (Rule 124).
79	func (m Model) GetFooterHeight() int {
80		height := 2 // empty line + info line
81		if m.showsResultTabs() {
82			height = 3 // tab bar + empty line + info line
83		}
84		if bar := m.activeFilterBar(); bar != nil {
85			height += bar.ExtraHeight() // Rule 136
86		}
87		return height
88	}
89	
90	// RenderFooter returns the footer content rendered below the viewport (Rule 124).
91	//
92	// The bar comes first whatever the state, because its top edge *is* the
93	// viewport's bottom border (Rule 136) — the same order oci_resources uses for
94	// the one bar it draws above a tab bar.
95	//
96	// It is resolved through activeFilterBar, like the height. The results branch
97	// drew no bar at all while GetFooterHeight counted one, so the router took two
98	// lines off the viewport and nothing filled them: the table's bottom border
99	// climbed the moment a severity token went on, and the tokens the user had just
100	// switched on were nowhere on screen.
101	func (m Model) RenderFooter(width int) string {
102		var parts []string
103		if bar := m.activeFilterBar(); bar != nil {
104			parts = append(parts, bar.View())

106		if m.showsResultTabs() {
107			parts = append(parts, theme.PadWithBg(theme.Bg(" ")+m.renderTabs(), width))
108		}
109		parts = append(parts, theme.EmptyLineBg(width), m.renderInfoLine(width))
110		return strings.Join(parts, "\n")

145	//
146	// A failed stage no longer takes it away, because nothing replaces the table
147	// any more: the tabs are what the results state is browsed with, and an empty
148	// one is an honest answer — the footer says which stage failed and where to

154	// renderInfoLine is the footer's message line, always rendered even when empty
155	// (Rule 124). The message expires on its own after three seconds (Rule 128).
156	func (m Model) renderInfoLine(width int) string {
157		return m.footer.View(width, m.status())
158	}

160	// status is what the footer says when no message is in flight.
161	//
162	// A stage that failed is a **state** of the result rather than an event: it is
163	// true for as long as the result is on screen, and a message would expire after
164	// three seconds — the distinction Rule 128 draws between the two. It carries
165	// the error level, because that is what happened, and it names the stages so
166	// the log can be searched for them.
167	func (m Model) status() sharedcomponents.Status {
168		if m.state == StateInventory {
169			return m.inventoryStatus()
170		}
171		// Which lines of a long detail are on screen: a state of the screen, derived
172		// here and never stored, so no timer can take it away (Rule 128).
173		if m.state == StateDetails {
174			if status, ok := m.verifyingStatus(); ok {
175				return status
176			}
177			if m.previewingStatus() {
178				return sharedcomponents.Status{Text: preparingFooter, Activity: true}
179			}
180			vp := m.detailsViewport
181			return sharedcomponents.Status{Text: scrollPosition(vp.YOffset(), vp.VisibleLineCount(), vp.TotalLineCount())}
182		}
183		// Ahead of the failed stages below: on this tab what is happening now is
184		// what the footer is for, and a stage that failed still shows on the others.
185		if status, ok := m.remediationStatus(); ok {
186			return status
187		}
188		if m.state != StateResults || m.result == nil || len(m.result.Errors) == 0 {
189			return sharedcomponents.Status{}
190		}
191		return sharedcomponents.Status{
192			Text:  failedStages(m.result.Errors) + " — check logs",
193			Level: sharedcomponents.LevelError,
194		}
195	}
196	
197	// inventoryStatus is the inventory footer: the selected row's own activity
198	// (its detail), composed with the batch progress or, while the caches are
199	// read, the load text. The load no longer hides the row: a failed row still
200	// says so under a ctrl+r.
201	func (m Model) inventoryStatus() sharedcomponents.Status {
202		st := sharedcomponents.Status{Text: sharedcomponents.JobsStatusLine(m.jobs, command.ViewSecurity)}
203		if m.inventoryLoading {
204			st.Text = "Loading scan inventory..."
205		}
206		moving := false
207		if row, ok := m.inventory.Selected(); ok {
208			a := m.rowActivity(row)
209			st.Detail = a.Detail
210			moving = a.State == indicator.Running || a.State == indicator.Queued
211		}
212		// The load and jobs work share the one activity dot; only a detail whose dot
213		// moves replaces it (a failed row's is fixed).
214		st.Activity = m.inventoryLoading ||
215			len(jobs.Unfinished(m.jobs)) > 0 && (!moving || st.Detail.IsZero())
216		return st
217	}
218	
219	// failedStages names what failed, reading the "<stage>: <reason>" that
220	// scan.recordStageError writes. The reason stays in the log: a footer is one
221	// line, and a tool's stderr is not.
222	func failedStages(errs []string) string {
223		stages := make([]string, 0, len(errs))
224		for _, e := range errs {
225			stage := e
226			if idx := strings.Index(e, ": "); idx != -1 {
227				stage = e[:idx]
228			}
229			stages = append(stages, stage)
230		}
231		return strings.Join(stages, ", ") + " failed"
232	}

234	// renderTabs renders the tab bar
235	func (m Model) renderTabs() string {
236		cve, secrets, licenses, misconfigs, ci := m.countFindingsByTab()
237	
238		return theme.RenderTabs([]theme.TabItem{
239			{Label: fmt.Sprintf("CVE (%d)", cve)},
240			{Label: fmt.Sprintf("Secrets (%d)", secrets)},
241			{Label: fmt.Sprintf("Licenses (%d)", licenses)},
242			{Label: fmt.Sprintf("Misconfig (%d)", misconfigs)},
243			// The count, like its four neighbours — not the letter. A letter in a
244			// column of counts would break the only thing the tab bar keeps
245			// aligned, and the grade already has a line of its own below.
246			{Label: fmt.Sprintf("CI (%d)", ci)},
247			{Label: m.remediationTabLabel()},
248		}, m.activeTab)
249	}

145	// GetHeaderInfo returns the key-value info for the header: the context, one
146	// count, and in the results how much of it is fixable.
147	//
148	// It used to carry seven fields in the results state, which is exactly the
149	// number buildInfoLines renders — an eighth would have been dropped in silence.
150	// Most of them had stopped earning their line:
151	//
152	//   - Trivy and Gitleaks versions answered "can I scan?", which the dashboard
153	//     already answers from shared.State.Tools, and which an inventory of past
154	//     scans is not about.
155	//   - Filter showed the severity filter, permanently reading ALL, and meaning
156	//     nothing on the Secrets tab or in the details.
157	//   - Secrets and Licenses duplicated the tab bar, which renders the same two
158	//     numbers a line below.
159	//
160	// Fixable came back on its own merits: it is the one figure that says what can
161	// be done, which none of the removed ones did.
162	//
163	// The context is what replaced them, and it is the one thing that was missing:
164	// the scan caches are scoped to a context, so the same inventory rows mean
165	// different things in two of them and look identical.
166	func (m Model) GetHeaderInfo(context string) []shortcut.HeaderInfo {
167		info := []shortcut.HeaderInfo{
168			{Key: "Context", Value: context, Style: theme.HeaderValueStyle},
169		}
170		if key, value, ok := m.headerCount(); ok {
171			info = append(info, shortcut.HeaderInfo{Key: key, Value: value, Style: theme.HeaderValueStyle})
172		}
173		if pss, ok := m.pssHeader(); ok {
174			info = append(info, pss)
175		}
176		if value, style, ok := m.headerFixable(); ok {
177			info = append(info, shortcut.HeaderInfo{Key: "Fixable", Value: value, Style: style})
178		}
179		if value, ok := m.headerUnrendered(); ok {
180			info = append(info, shortcut.HeaderInfo{Key: "Not rendered", Value: value, Style: theme.HeaderValueStyle})
181		}
182		if sig, ok := m.signatureHeader(); ok {
183			info = append(info, sig)
184		}
185		return info
186	}
187	
188	// headerUnrendered is how many Helm charts and Kustomize overlays the schema
189	// stage could not look at, for want of helm or kustomize (§3.80). Without it a
190	// repository of charts would read as schema-clean when nothing was checked.
191	// Absent when there are none — it is not a count of findings, and a "0" on
192	// every result would be noise about a stage most repositories do not need.
193	func (m Model) headerUnrendered() (string, bool) {
194		if (m.state != StateResults && m.state != StateDetails) || m.result == nil || len(m.result.K8sUnrendered) == 0 {
195			return "", false
196		}
197		return strconv.Itoa(len(m.result.K8sUnrendered)) + " (install helm / kustomize)", true
198	}
199	
200	// headerFixable is how many of the vulnerabilities have a fixed version, split
201	// by what has to move: "12 (8 base, 4 deps)". It is the one number that says
202	// what can be done about the findings, which the count above does not. Like the
203	// count, it is absent where the state is a list of nothing, and it is present
204	// on both sides of the results/details step so the header does not change
205	// under the reader (Rule 130).
206	func (m Model) headerFixable() (string, lipgloss.Style, bool) {
207		if (m.state != StateResults && m.state != StateDetails) || m.result == nil {
208			return "", lipgloss.Style{}, false
209		}
210		s := remediation.Summarize(m.result.Findings)
211		if s.Fixable() == 0 {
212			return "0", theme.DimStyle, true
213		}
214		var parts []string
215		if s.BaseImage > 0 {
216			parts = append(parts, strconv.Itoa(s.BaseImage)+" base")
217		}
218		if s.Dependencies > 0 {
219			parts = append(parts, strconv.Itoa(s.Dependencies)+" deps")
220		}
221		if s.Unclassified > 0 {
222			parts = append(parts, strconv.Itoa(s.Unclassified)+" unclassified")
223		}
224		return strconv.Itoa(s.Fixable()) + " (" + strings.Join(parts, ", ") + ")", theme.HeaderValueStyle, true
225	}

227	// headerCount is the one number the header shows, named for whatever the state
228	// is actually a list of. The form and the scanning screen are lists of nothing,
229	// and report no count rather than a zero.
230	func (m Model) headerCount() (key, value string, ok bool) {
231		switch m.state {
232		case StateInventory:
233			return "Targets", strconv.Itoa(len(m.inventory.Items())), true
234		case StateResults, StateDetails:
235			if m.result == nil {
236				return "", "", false
237			}
238			return "Findings", strconv.Itoa(m.result.TotalFindings()), true
239		}
240		return "", "", false
241	}

Its findings have 'context' as their source.\nBase image signatures: DevDesk's own check too, run with the Misconfiguration category unless Verify image signatures is unticked (scan tab of the configuration view). Every FROM of every Dockerfile — a build stage included, since a compromised builder writes the binary that ships — is checked against your rules (~/.devdesk/trust.yaml) and the built-in ones, with cosign. A signature by an unexpected identity is CRITICAL (DEVDESK-SIG-001); no accepted signature where a rule requires one is HIGH (DEVDESK-SIG-002). Only a proven violation is a finding: an image no rule covers says nothing, and a check that could not run under one of your rules is reported as an error of the scan. Its findings have 'signature' as their source, and the Remediation tab lists candidates whose signature holds.\nLicense Scan: analyzes dependency licenses (Trivy).\nCI Score: grades a repository's pipeline configuration (plumber), for this context's forge only — a repository hosted elsewhere is not graded rather than graded without credentials. The grade is on the CI tab, above the issues; a run that could not collect everything says so instead of showing a letter.",
283				},
284				{
285					Title: "Targets",
286					Body:  "A target is a Docker image or a repository under the configured workspaces directory. Images are scanned from the OCI resources view (:oci) and repositories from the workspaces view (:w); both write to the caches this inventory reads, so anything scanned anywhere appears here and can be rescanned from here.",
287				},
288				{
289					Title: "Scan Options",
290					Body:  "Every option lives in the configuration view (:cfg), scan tab: which scanners run, whether to use a Trivy server, custom binaries or images, whether to ignore unfixed or end-of-life findings, a custom .gitleaks.toml, and whether Gitleaks reads the full git history. A rescan started here reads them at the moment it runs.",
291				},
292				{
293					Title: "Results",
294					Body:  "Results are displayed by tab (CVE, Secrets, Licenses, Misconfig). Every finding belongs to exactly one tab, and the count on each label is the same number the scan recorded. Severity is filtered with c, h, m and l — they are cumulative, so c and h together ask for CRITICAL or HIGH, which a threshold could not express. The active ones are shown in the bar under the table, beside the search field. '.' cycles the sort column and '/' searches. The Fixable figure in the header counts the vulnerabilities that have a fixed version, split into base image packages (cleared by upgrading the image's packages or moving to a newer base image) and application dependencies (cleared only by bumping the dependency itself); a result scanned before this was recorded shows its findings as unclassified until the next scan. On the Misconfigurations tab a File column shows where each finding is, as a path relative to the scanned directory (a path under the scanner container's /scan mount is shortened to its relative form, and any other absolute path under your home directory starts with ~); it is the first column dropped on a narrow terminal, and a long path loses its start, not its file name. Press Enter to view finding details (see Finding details), which name the package kind and the command that moves it. For secrets, X adds a finding to .gitleaksignore; it is offered for Gitleaks findings only, since that file is matched on a Gitleaks fingerprint a Trivy secret does not have.\nEsc returns to the inventory, or to the list the results were opened from.",
295				},
296				{
297					Title: "Finding details",
298					Body: "The detail of a finding puts what to do before why: its severity, ID and title (always one line, cut with an ellipsis), then the Fix block and what the fix would write, then Why, Output and Refs. It is one column of at most 110 cells. A section with nothing to say is left out.\n" +
299						"Fix is always there and says the status in words, one of six. 'Built-in fix available': DevDesk can write the fix for this rule. 'Built-in fix unavailable: <reason>': the rule has a built-in fix and it declines this instance, for the reason given. 'Manual': the finding tells how to fix it by hand, which includes a vulnerability with a fixed version. 'No fix published': a vulnerability with no fixed version. 'Cannot fix here': a misconfiguration of an image, whose files are inside it and cannot be written. 'No guidance available': nothing tells how to fix it. For a misconfiguration the status is the same answer the shortcut for writing a fix gives.\n" +
300						"Under Fix, with no blank line: Where is the file and line, then the package, the CI job, its script line and the matched text when the finding has them. Do is the numbered steps (the ones DevDesk writes for the findings it builds itself, such as a chart or overlay that does not render, a schema or helm lint message, or a secret, come first), then the resolution the scanner gave, word for word. Run is the command, on one line, cut with an ellipsis when it is wider than the column; DevDesk shows it and never runs it. Repro, for a finding DevDesk built from a tool that ran on this machine, is the one command that reproduces it, to run from the scanned directory, without the arguments you set for the tool; when the tool ran in a container the line says there is none, and no line is shown when no plain command says it (a path with a space, a finding in rendered output). A sentence such as 'Update foo to 1.2', for an ecosystem DevDesk has no command for, is a step under Do, never a command. So is a command that is not plain words (a line break, a control character, a shell metacharacter such as ; | & $ or a quote): its text is under Do, cleaned, and Y cannot copy it. Effect is what the fix does, or 'Fixed in <version>', and Warning is what the built-in fix may break.\n" +
301						"Change is what the built-in fix would write, shown before you ask for it: the file it edits, then its diff (+ for an added line, - for a removed one, @@ for where a hunk starts), at most 8 rows with '… N more lines' after them (the Ctrl+O confirmation shows every row), then Git: what git will and will not be able to undo. It is computed when the detail opens, and again after a re-scan; the footer says 'Preparing the change preview...' meanwhile. A vulnerability with a fixed version shows the move ('libfoo 0.8.0 -> 0.17.0') and never a diff, since DevDesk does not write lockfiles. Where DevDesk cannot write the fix (a finding it has no rule for, an image, a rule that declines this instance) it says 'none: DevDesk cannot write this fix'. A file written after the scan ended shows no diff, only 'stale preview', and Ctrl+O is greyed with the same reason until a re-scan: the lines the scan reported may no longer be the file's. A preview that could not be computed says so, and Ctrl+O stays available, since it computes the fix again. Rows longer than the column are cut with an ellipsis; the confirmation has them whole.\n" +
302						"Why holds the Description, the Pod Security profile, the Source and the Type. Output is what the scanner said about this instance, which tells two findings of one rule apart: at most 8 lines of at most 110 cells, then '… N more lines'; the rest is in the log. An Output that only repeats the title or the description is not shown. Refs lists the references.\n" +
303						"The detail has six keys, the same for every finding, each greyed with its reason in the footer when it has nothing to act on. Esc goes back. W opens the first reference. Enter opens the finding's file in the viewer (O there opens the IDE, esc comes back to the detail); whether the file exists is for the viewer to say, and a path outside the scanned directory, a file reached through a link that leaves it, or a target that is an image, is refused. Ctrl+O applies the built-in fix of this finding, with the same preview, the same confirmation that defaults to No, the same write and the same re-scan as the Misconfigurations tab; while the re-scan runs the footer says so, and when it ends the detail shows the finding as the re-scan read it, or closes if the finding is gone, with the verdict in the footer. Y copies the command under Run, or else the Repro line, to the clipboard, whole even when the screen cuts it; DevDesk never runs a command. X adds a Gitleaks secret to .gitleaksignore, after a confirmation. Each acts on the finding on screen, not on the row behind it.\n" +
304						"Paths in the title, Where and Output are shown relative to the scanned directory (an absolute path under your home directory starts with ~); the finding itself is not changed.\n" +
305						"When the detail is taller than the viewport, the footer says which lines are on screen: 'Lines a-b of N'. A long detail scrolls with the arrows, page keys, Home and End.",
306				},
307				{
308					Title: "Pod Security",
309					Body: "On the Misconfigurations tab, a Kubernetes finding that a Pod Security Standards profile requires starts its title with that profile: baseline or restricted. The label is there under every setting. restricted includes baseline, so a restricted finding is one the baseline profile does not ask for.\n" +
310						"The profile comes from a table of Trivy's rules kept in DevDesk, checked against Trivy's own output. A rule the table lacks but whose reference carries a #baseline or #restricted anchor is labelled with it and marked '(from Trivy, no fix)': the profile is Trivy's, and DevDesk offers no fix for it. A rule that links the standard without an anchor, or not at all, has no label. KSV-0104 is baseline when the profile is explicitly Unconfined and restricted when none is set, read from the manifest at scan time; a result scanned before that, or a file changed since, counts as baseline.\n" +
311						"scan.pss_profile (scan tab of the configuration view) is all, baseline or restricted, and all by default. Under baseline or restricted, p hides what that profile does not require, and the header says the profile, the state of the filter and how many findings it hides. The filter is off whenever the tab opens, and p is greyed, with the reason, under all or elsewhere than the Misconfigurations tab. A value outside the three is read as all, with a warning on entering the tab.\n" +
312						"When the filter leaves no Pod Security finding, the header says 'no violation detected by Trivy for <profile>': that is what one scanner found in these manifests, not proof of compliance.",
313				},
314				{
315					Title: "Remediation",
316					Body: "For a repository, this tab reads the Dockerfiles under it and lists each base image — every stage, since a vulnerability in a build stage can reach the image that ships — with the newer tags it could move to. Candidates keep the image's variant (alpine stays alpine, slim stays slim) and its precision (3.18 is offered 3.21, not 3.21.1); by default they stay on the same major version, and the scan tab of the configuration view (Base image bumps) lets them take the next one.\nNothing is measured until you press S: each image is scanned straight from its registry, without being pulled, and the counts are kept for 24 hours. The vs now column is the change in CRITICAL plus HIGH against the image as written; negative is better. A candidate is a proposal with its evidence — the scan says the CVEs are gone, not that the application still runs on the new base.\nThe Update column puts an arrow on a base image whose registry has something newer: a later patch tag, or new content behind the same tag (the arrow alone — a new build) — compared with the digest the Dockerfile pins, or with the image the engine holds under that name; one the engine does not hold only gets the patch side, and shows a cloud (not local). The other states, each an icon: a check mark (up to date), an hourglass (no answer yet), a question mark in a circle (the registry did not answer), a pin (a digest with no tag, which cannot move). The registries are asked in the background when the tab opens, and each answer is kept 6 hours.\nA floating tag — latest, an untagged reference, main, a codename, or a vendor tag rebuilt in place such as Docker Hardened Images' — has no version to move to, so it lists no candidates and says so. Its count is of what the tag pointed to when it was scanned, and the registry may have replaced that since: S scans it again every time, whatever its age, rather than trusting the 24 hours. Nothing is written for it — pinning it by digest would stop it following upstream fixes.\nAn image scan has no Dockerfile, so the tab is empty for one.\nChoosing: space picks the candidate under the cursor for its stage — only one that has been scanned, since a bump is proposed with its evidence — and Enter shows what the choices would change. Ctrl+O writes them, and only when you ask: it lists each file and line, and says what git will be able to undo (a clean tracked file can be reverted with git checkout; one with uncommitted changes cannot without losing them; an untracked file or one outside a repository cannot at all). The answer defaults to No. Only the image reference changes — comments, line endings and the rest of the file are untouched — and DevDesk makes no commit, branch or push. A file that changed since the diff was computed is refused, not overwritten. A reference pinned by digest loses its pin, which the modal says. A stage that reads its image from an ARG changes that ARG's default, and a --build-arg on the command line can still override it.\n" +
317						"The Sig column is each image's signature (§3.82), checked in the background when the tab opens: the base image against your rules (~/.devdesk/trust.yaml) and the built-in ones, a candidate also against whoever signed that base. A check mark is a proven signature, a dash no rule to check against, an hourglass a check still running. A red cross is refused — an unexpected identity, or no signature where a rule asks for one: the candidate stays listed, since a tag republished by someone else is worth seeing, but space will not choose it and says which rule refused it. An orange sign warns — unsigned where nothing required it, or a check that could not run: it can be chosen, and the Ctrl+O confirmation repeats the warning. A verdict that arrives after you chose releases the choice. Turn the check off per context by unticking Verify image signatures (scan tab of the configuration view); the header then says Signatures: off.",
318				},
319				{
320					Title: "Command Logging",
321					Body:  "Executed scanner commands are logged to the application log file (~/.devdesk/devdesk.log).",
322				},
323				{
324					Title: "Prerequisites",
325					Body:  "Trivy and Gitleaks must be installed (local binary or Docker image). Whether each one is available is shown on the dashboard; a scan that could run no scanner at all reports that rather than returning an empty result.",
326				},
327			},
328		}
329	}

1	package security
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"strings"
6	
7		tea "charm.land/bubbletea/v2"
8		"charm.land/lipgloss/v2"
9	
10		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/command"
11		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/jobs"
12		sharedcomponents "github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/components"
13		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/indicator"
14		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
15	)
16	
17	// View is the Bubble Tea v2 face of Render: the content only. The terminal
18	// state (alternate screen, colours) belongs to whoever owns the program.
19	func (m Model) View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }
20	
21	// Render renders the UI
22	func (m Model) Render() string {
23		// Show whichever modal is active (Rule 112: modals confirm, forms fill the
24		// viewport).
25		if modal := m.modalView(); modal != "" {
26			return lipgloss.Place(
27				m.width, m.height,
28				lipgloss.Center, lipgloss.Center,
29				modal,
30				lipgloss.WithWhitespaceStyle(lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground)),
31			)
32		}
33	
34		switch m.state {
35		case StateInventory:
36			return m.renderInventoryView()
37		case StateResults:
38			return m.renderResultsView()
39		case StateDetails:
40			return m.renderDetailsView()
41		}
42		return ""
43	}
44	
45	// renderResultsView renders the results summary
46	func (m Model) renderResultsView() string {
47		if m.result == nil {
48			return "No results"
49		}
50	
51		// A stage that failed is **not** rendered here. It goes to the log, and the
52		// footer says to look there (Rule 128).
53		//
54		// It used to be a panel that replaced the whole table whenever
55		// Result.Errors was non-empty, on the stated grounds that a failed scan has
56		// no partial results to browse. That held while an error meant nothing had
57		// run; it stopped holding the day a stage could fail beside three that
58		// succeeded, and a plumber failure then took every CVE and every secret
59		// down with it. Folding it to a banner above the table only moved the
60		// problem — five tabs, permanently, for a message read once — and a tool's
61		// stderr reformatted for a viewport is what a log is for.
62		//
63		// Nothing is lost by it: internal/scan logs every stage failure at the
64		// point it records one, which it did not do before. The only copy of the
65		// reason used to be on screen.
66		//
67		// The grade had a line of its own above the table on the CI tab, and it is
68		// gone: it cost that tab two of its rows — the line and its blank — on
69		// every open, to state a letter the inventory's own CI column carries per
70		// target. A tab that shows fewer findings than its four neighbours, for a
71		// value already on the previous screen, is not a trade worth making.
72		if m.activeTab == TabRemediation {
73			return m.remediation.table.View()
74		}
75		return m.findingsTable.View()
76	}
77	
78	// GetFooterHeight returns the footer height for this view (Rule 124).
79	func (m Model) GetFooterHeight() int {
80		height := 2 // empty line + info line
81		if m.showsResultTabs() {
82			height = 3 // tab bar + empty line + info line
83		}
84		if bar := m.activeFilterBar(); bar != nil {
85			height += bar.ExtraHeight() // Rule 136
86		}
87		return height
88	}
89	
90	// RenderFooter returns the footer content rendered below the viewport (Rule 124).
91	//
92	// The bar comes first whatever the state, because its top edge *is* the
93	// viewport's bottom border (Rule 136) — the same order oci_resources uses for
94	// the one bar it draws above a tab bar.
95	//
96	// It is resolved through activeFilterBar, like the height. The results branch
97	// drew no bar at all while GetFooterHeight counted one, so the router took two
98	// lines off the viewport and nothing filled them: the table's bottom border
99	// climbed the moment a severity token went on, and the tokens the user had just
100	// switched on were nowhere on screen.
101	func (m Model) RenderFooter(width int) string {
102		var parts []string
103		if bar := m.activeFilterBar(); bar != nil {
104			parts = append(parts, bar.View())
105		}
106		if m.showsResultTabs() {
107			parts = append(parts, theme.PadWithBg(theme.Bg(" ")+m.renderTabs(), width))
108		}
109		parts = append(parts, theme.EmptyLineBg(width), m.renderInfoLine(width))
110		return strings.Join(parts, "\n")
111	}
112	
113	// modalView renders whichever modal is open, or "" when none is.
114	func (m Model) modalView() string {
115		switch {
116		case m.confirmModal != nil:
117			return m.confirmModal.View()
118		case m.scanAllModal != nil:
119			return m.scanAllModal.View()
120		}
121		return ""
122	}
123	
124	// activeFilterBar is the bar of whichever table is on screen, or nil when the
125	// state has no table. One resolution rather than three, so GetFooterHeight and
126	// RenderFooter cannot disagree about whether the bar is there — which is the
127	// one way to make Rule 124's arithmetic wrong by a line.
128	func (m Model) activeFilterBar() *sharedcomponents.FilterBar {
129		var bar *sharedcomponents.FilterBar
130		switch {
131		case m.state == StateInventory:
132			bar = m.inventory.FilterBar()
133		case m.showsResultTabs() && m.activeTab != TabRemediation:
134			// The Remediation tab has a table of its own and no filter: the bar
135			// belongs to the findings table behind it.
136			bar = m.findingsTable.FilterBar()
137		}
138		if bar == nil || !bar.IsVisible() {
139			return nil
140		}
141		return bar
142	}
143	
144	// showsResultTabs reports whether the findings tab bar is on screen.
145	//
146	// A failed stage no longer takes it away, because nothing replaces the table
147	// any more: the tabs are what the results state is browsed with, and an empty
148	// one is an honest answer — the footer says which stage failed and where to
149	// read why.
150	func (m Model) showsResultTabs() bool {
151		return m.state == StateResults && m.result != nil
152	}
153	
154	// renderInfoLine is the footer's message line, always rendered even when empty
155	// (Rule 124). The message expires on its own after three seconds (Rule 128).
156	func (m Model) renderInfoLine(width int) string {
157		return m.footer.View(width, m.status())
158	}
159	
160	// status is what the footer says when no message is in flight.
161	//
162	// A stage that failed is a **state** of the result rather than an event: it is
163	// true for as long as the result is on screen, and a message would expire after
164	// three seconds — the distinction Rule 128 draws between the two. It carries
165	// the error level, because that is what happened, and it names the stages so
166	// the log can be searched for them.
167	func (m Model) status() sharedcomponents.Status {
168		if m.state == StateInventory {
169			return m.inventoryStatus()
170		}
171		// Which lines of a long detail are on screen: a state of the screen, derived
172		// here and never stored, so no timer can take it away (Rule 128).
173		if m.state == StateDetails {
174			if status, ok := m.verifyingStatus(); ok {
175				return status
176			}
177			if m.previewingStatus() {
178				return sharedcomponents.Status{Text: preparingFooter, Activity: true}
179			}
180			vp := m.detailsViewport
181			return sharedcomponents.Status{Text: scrollPosition(vp.YOffset(), vp.VisibleLineCount(), vp.TotalLineCount())}
182		}
183		// Ahead of the failed stages below: on this tab what is happening now is
184		// what the footer is for, and a stage that failed still shows on the others.
185		if status, ok := m.remediationStatus(); ok {
186			return status
187		}
188		if m.state != StateResults || m.result == nil || len(m.result.Errors) == 0 {
189			return sharedcomponents.Status{}
190		}
191		return sharedcomponents.Status{
192			Text:  failedStages(m.result.Errors) + " — check logs",
193			Level: sharedcomponents.LevelError,
194		}
195	}
196	
197	// inventoryStatus is the inventory footer: the selected row's own activity
198	// (its detail), composed with the batch progress or, while the caches are
199	// read, the load text. The load no longer hides the row: a failed row still
200	// says so under a ctrl+r.
201	func (m Model) inventoryStatus() sharedcomponents.Status {
202		st := sharedcomponents.Status{Text: sharedcomponents.JobsStatusLine(m.jobs, command.ViewSecurity)}
203		if m.inventoryLoading {
204			st.Text = "Loading scan inventory..."
205		}
206		moving := false
207		if row, ok := m.inventory.Selected(); ok {
208			a := m.rowActivity(row)
209			st.Detail = a.Detail
210			moving = a.State == indicator.Running || a.State == indicator.Queued
211		}
212		// The load and jobs work share the one activity dot; only a detail whose dot
213		// moves replaces it (a failed row's is fixed).
214		st.Activity = m.inventoryLoading ||
215			len(jobs.Unfinished(m.jobs)) > 0 && (!moving || st.Detail.IsZero())
216		return st
217	}
218	
219	// failedStages names what failed, reading the "<stage>: <reason>" that
220	// scan.recordStageError writes. The reason stays in the log: a footer is one
221	// line, and a tool's stderr is not.
222	func failedStages(errs []string) string {
223		stages := make([]string, 0, len(errs))
224		for _, e := range errs {
225			stage := e
226			if idx := strings.Index(e, ": "); idx != -1 {
227				stage = e[:idx]
228			}
229			stages = append(stages, stage)
230		}
231		return strings.Join(stages, ", ") + " failed"
232	}
233	
234	// renderTabs renders the tab bar
235	func (m Model) renderTabs() string {
236		cve, secrets, licenses, misconfigs, ci := m.countFindingsByTab()
237	
238		return theme.RenderTabs([]theme.TabItem{
239			{Label: fmt.Sprintf("CVE (%d)", cve)},
240			{Label: fmt.Sprintf("Secrets (%d)", secrets)},
241			{Label: fmt.Sprintf("Licenses (%d)", licenses)},
242			{Label: fmt.Sprintf("Misconfig (%d)", misconfigs)},
243			// The count, like its four neighbours — not the letter. A letter in a
244			// column of counts would break the only thing the tab bar keeps
245			// aligned, and the grade already has a line of its own below.
246			{Label: fmt.Sprintf("CI (%d)", ci)},
247			{Label: m.remediationTabLabel()},
248		}, m.activeTab)
249	}

1	package security
2	
3	import (
4		"strconv"
5		"strings"
6	
7		"charm.land/lipgloss/v2"
8	
9		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/remediation"
10		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/help"
11		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/indicator"
12		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/keymap"
13		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/shortcut"
14		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
15	)
16	
17	func (m Model) GetShortcuts() shortcut.Shortcuts {
18		switch m.state {
19		case StateInventory:
20			return m.inventoryShortcuts()
21		case StateResults:
22			return m.resultsShortcuts()
23		case StateDetails:
24			return m.detailsShortcuts()
25		}
26		return nil
27	}
28	
29	// detailsShortcuts is the detail's column: the same six keys for every finding,
30	// each greyed when it has nothing to act on (Rule 130). Every availability is
31	// computed from the finding on screen alone, so the header reads no file. The
32	// descriptions are at most ten cells: the column is 19 cells wide at 80 columns
33	// and `<ctrl+o>` takes nine of them.
34	func (m Model) detailsShortcuts() shortcut.Shortcuts {
35		// A finding with no published reference is the same screen as one with three,
36		// so W is greyed rather than dropped. keymap.Web is what handleDetailsState
37		// binds: a key advertised under another name would do nothing.
38		f := m.selectedFinding
39		return []shortcut.Shortcut{
40			{Key: "esc", Description: "Back"},
41			{Key: keymap.Web, Description: "Open ref", Disabled: f == nil || len(f.References) == 0},
42			{Key: "enter", Description: "Open file", Disabled: !m.canOpenFindingFile().Enabled()},
43			{Key: writeRemediationKey, Description: "Apply fix", Disabled: !m.canFixMisconfig().Enabled()},
44			{Key: keymap.Copy, Description: "Copy cmd", Disabled: !m.canCopyFixCommand().Enabled()},
45			{Key: keymap.Exclude, Description: "Exclude", Disabled: !m.canExclude().Enabled()},
46		}
47	}
48	
49	// resultsShortcuts advertises the findings table's own keys.
50	//
51	// The four severity toggles were bound and unadvertised — a user had to open
52	// the help to learn the view filtered at all — and `.` was offered on three
53	// tabs out of four, from back when it cycled the severity floor. It is the sort

145	// GetHeaderInfo returns the key-value info for the header: the context, one
146	// count, and in the results how much of it is fixable.
147	//
148	// It used to carry seven fields in the results state, which is exactly the
149	// number buildInfoLines renders — an eighth would have been dropped in silence.
150	// Most of them had stopped earning their line:
151	//
152	//   - Trivy and Gitleaks versions answered "can I scan?", which the dashboard
153	//     already answers from shared.State.Tools, and which an inventory of past
154	//     scans is not about.
155	//   - Filter showed the severity filter, permanently reading ALL, and meaning
156	//     nothing on the Secrets tab or in the details.
157	//   - Secrets and Licenses duplicated the tab bar, which renders the same two
158	//     numbers a line below.
159	//
160	// Fixable came back on its own merits: it is the one figure that says what can
161	// be done, which none of the removed ones did.
162	//
163	// The context is what replaced them, and it is the one thing that was missing:
164	// the scan caches are scoped to a context, so the same inventory rows mean
165	// different things in two of them and look identical.
166	func (m Model) GetHeaderInfo(context string) []shortcut.HeaderInfo {
167		info := []shortcut.HeaderInfo{
168			{Key: "Context", Value: context, Style: theme.HeaderValueStyle},
169		}
170		if key, value, ok := m.headerCount(); ok {
171			info = append(info, shortcut.HeaderInfo{Key: key, Value: value, Style: theme.HeaderValueStyle})
172		}
173		if pss, ok := m.pssHeader(); ok {
174			info = append(info, pss)
175		}
176		if value, style, ok := m.headerFixable(); ok {
177			info = append(info, shortcut.HeaderInfo{Key: "Fixable", Value: value, Style: style})
178		}
179		if value, ok := m.headerUnrendered(); ok {
180			info = append(info, shortcut.HeaderInfo{Key: "Not rendered", Value: value, Style: theme.HeaderValueStyle})
181		}
182		if sig, ok := m.signatureHeader(); ok {
183			info = append(info, sig)
184		}
185		return info
186	}

188	// headerUnrendered is how many Helm charts and Kustomize overlays the schema
189	// stage could not look at, for want of helm or kustomize (§3.80). Without it a
190	// repository of charts would read as schema-clean when nothing was checked.
191	// Absent when there are none — it is not a count of findings, and a "0" on
192	// every result would be noise about a stage most repositories do not need.
193	func (m Model) headerUnrendered() (string, bool) {
194		if (m.state != StateResults && m.state != StateDetails) || m.result == nil || len(m.result.K8sUnrendered) == 0 {
195			return "", false
196		}
197		return strconv.Itoa(len(m.result.K8sUnrendered)) + " (install helm / kustomize)", true
198	}
199	
200	// headerFixable is how many of the vulnerabilities have a fixed version, split
201	// by what has to move: "12 (8 base, 4 deps)". It is the one number that says
202	// what can be done about the findings, which the count above does not. Like the
203	// count, it is absent where the state is a list of nothing, and it is present
204	// on both sides of the results/details step so the header does not change
205	// under the reader (Rule 130).
206	func (m Model) headerFixable() (string, lipgloss.Style, bool) {
207		if (m.state != StateResults && m.state != StateDetails) || m.result == nil {
208			return "", lipgloss.Style{}, false
209		}
210		s := remediation.Summarize(m.result.Findings)
211		if s.Fixable() == 0 {
212			return "0", theme.DimStyle, true
213		}
214		var parts []string
215		if s.BaseImage > 0 {
216			parts = append(parts, strconv.Itoa(s.BaseImage)+" base")
217		}
218		if s.Dependencies > 0 {
219			parts = append(parts, strconv.Itoa(s.Dependencies)+" deps")
220		}
221		if s.Unclassified > 0 {
222			parts = append(parts, strconv.Itoa(s.Unclassified)+" unclassified")
223		}
224		return strconv.Itoa(s.Fixable()) + " (" + strings.Join(parts, ", ") + ")", theme.HeaderValueStyle, true
225	}

227	// headerCount is the one number the header shows, named for whatever the state
228	// is actually a list of. The form and the scanning screen are lists of nothing,
229	// and report no count rather than a zero.
230	func (m Model) headerCount() (key, value string, ok bool) {
231		switch m.state {
232		case StateInventory:
233			return "Targets", strconv.Itoa(len(m.inventory.Items())), true
234		case StateResults, StateDetails:
235			if m.result == nil {
236				return "", "", false
237			}
238			return "Findings", strconv.Itoa(m.result.TotalFindings()), true
239		}
240		return "", "", false
241	}
